messages:
Alice Chen: Heads-up — we're seeing a spike in contract rejects for the action route `/v1/actions/order_suggest`. Console shows `validation_fail` counter +220% in the last 5m. Is this a strictness rollout or a model behaviour change?

ops-alert-bot: ALERT: metric `response_contract_reject` increased by 220% on route /v1/actions/order_suggest (5m window). Dashboard: https://console.internal/redwood/d/route-contracts?panel=order_suggest

Miguel Alvarez: Looking now. Samples show tool responses missing the `items` array and sometimes returning `results` as a string. Example payload:```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "meta": { "seed": 42 },
  "results": "suggestion1; suggestion2"
}```
This fails the route schema which expects `items: [object]`.

Sofia Li: We flipped the canary model to `open-xyz-2` yesterday; that model is more generative and occasionally returns freeform fields. We also merged the strict-check change (commit 6aa2) last week. Could be the intersection of both.

Alice Chen: We should avoid customer-facing errors. Options: 1) relax schema enforcement for this route, 2) rollback the strict-check canary, 3) add an adapter that coerces these responses into the expected shape. Thoughts on least-risky path?

Miguel Alvarez: We already have a `soft_validation=true` flag per-route but it's not enabled for order_suggest. Flipping it would change rejections into `soft_accept` and emit telemetry tag `validation_mode:soft`.

Raj Patel: If we relax, any billing/quota implications? Also per incident policy, if user-facing errors >1% we need to page.

Sofia Li: Quick proposal: enable `soft_validation` + deploy a tiny coercer that maps `results` -> `items` when `results` is a string. Log a reason code `coerce_results_to_items`. It buys us time while we assess model behavior.

Miguel Alvarez: I created a local patch that coerces and increments `contract_coerce_count`. It also attaches an example sample to the logs for inspection. No schema change upstream, just adapter-level translation.

Alice Chen: Good. Add a dashboard tile comparing `contract_reject` vs `contract_coerce_count` and set an alert if `contract_coerce_count` > 5% of total requests for 10m. We want visibility into silent fixes.

ops-alert-bot: NOTE: Scheduled deploy window open at 20:30 UTC. Canary rollback policy: auto-rollback on increased p95 latency or contract_reject rate.

Raj Patel: :thumbsup: I'll monitor p95 and the error budget. If latency jumps > 50ms we rollback manually.

Sofia Li: I'll roll a 10% canary with `soft_validation=true` + coercer (10% -> 50% -> 100%). Auto-rollback thresholds: contract_reject increase > 10% absolute or coerce_count > 8% sustained.

Miguel Alvarez: UX/Console note: we should surface `validation_mode` and `coerce_reason` as event types on the per-route timeline so product owners can inspect examples. I'll file a small UX ticket.

Alice Chen: OK. If no objections I'll flip the flag at ~20:35 and watch metrics. Share PR link and dashboard snapshot in this thread.

Raj Patel: No objections. Will escalate if threshold breached.

Miguel Alvarez: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/PR/1234 — includes coercer, metric emission, and feature-flag toggle.

Sofia Li: Deployed canary in us-west-2 @20:36. Early telemetry: `contract_reject` down ~90% on canary slice, `contract_coerce_count` ~0.8% of requests. Latency p95 unchanged.

Alice Chen: Nice. Leave the flag for 1 hour then re-evaluate. Thanks team. :rocket:
